# BuzzFeed

**Digital media company.** Cited in [[ai-engineering-ch08-dataset-engineering|*AI Engineering* Ch 8]] for a 2023 cost-reduction case study: finetuned [[FlanT5|Flan-T5]] using [[lora|LoRA]] on examples generated by [[openai|OpenAI]]'s text-davinci-003, **reducing inference cost by 80%**.

## The case study

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model | [[FlanT5\|Flan-T5]] |
| Adaptation method | [[lora\|LoRA]] |
| Training data | Generated by text-davinci-003 |
| Result | 80% inference cost reduction |
| Caveat | "Unclear how well the model performed" (Ch 8) |

## Why Ch 8 cites it

BuzzFeed is one of the chapter's [[knowledgedistillation|distillation]] examples — using synthetic data from a more expensive teacher (text-davinci-003) to finetune a cheaper student (Flan-T5+LoRA). The 80% cost-reduction number is the headline; Huyen's hedge about output quality is the caution.

## Connections

- [[knowledgedistillation]] — the operation BuzzFeed implemented.
- [[lora|LoRA]] — the PEFT method.
- [[FlanT5]] — the base model.
- [[openai|OpenAI]] — the teacher's lab.
- [[AIPoweredDataSynthesis]] — the data-generation technique.
- [[ai-engineering-ch08-dataset-engineering]] — primary source.
